title: OpenAI publishes its internal pretraining progress and proposes industry-wide "common limits"
description:
OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki (@merettm) published "Perplexity and Intelligence," sharing OpenAI's internal log-perplexity measurements and proposing perplexity as a shared metric across labs. Per summaries of the post, GPT-3.5 sat near ~0.99 and GPT-4 near ~0.91, losses below 0.8 brought cybersecurity and math capabilities, an unreleased internal model is already below GPT-6.2 Astra, and he expects further transformative capabilities around ~0.68–0.7, possibly an "avalanche" of pretraining advances as soon as 2027. He proposes common limits that labs would not cross until AI monitoring reaches a concrete milestone, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors; Sam Altman called it "the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile."

Why it matters: OpenAI is publicly inviting rival labs to agree on a measurable pause point, which could shape how frontier training is paced and regulated.

description:

With real inference latency counted, the best success rate was 44%, and 36% when required to succeed in all three trials. More reasoning had mixed effects, because a better decision can arrive too late.

Why it matters: Agents for driving, games or live operations need to be fast as well as smart, and most benchmarks ignore speed.

He said Tesla has had a near pixel-perfect world model for synthetic training data since last year, that latency is still a bit high due to compute limits, and that the coming AI5 chip has roughly 12 times more compute.

Why it matters: It shows a real-time generative world model running on car hardware, and hints at how much more Tesla expects from its next chip.

title: Yann LeCun co-authors a paper on getting JEPA world models to keep a usable map for planning
description:
A new paper from Yann LeCun and co-authors finds that common ways of stopping JEPA models from collapsing tend to keep either smooth geometry (useful for measuring progress toward a goal) or object content, but not both. Their fix, SVReg, steps in only when the spread of the model's representations gets too small, and the authors then refined it after finding a content–geometry tradeoff.

Why it matters: Planning in a learned latent space is LeCun's main alternative to LLMs, and this addresses a known weak spot.

title: Sean Stone’s 10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul
description:
10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul explores what it means to remain fully human in an age increasingly defined by technology, optimization, and artificial intelligence. While modern civilization has expanded humanity’s power and capability, it has done little to eliminate suffering, grief, fear, or the search for meaning. This book argues that life’s deepest questions cannot be answered through efficiency or control. Instead, genuine growth emerges through a series of essential initiations—moments of collapse, surrender, loss, rest, and devotion that shape the soul. Blending mythology, philosophy, memoir, and poetic reflection, it offers a timeless framework for navigating the emotional and spiritual disorientation of modern life.

Structured around ten symbolic “gates,” the book reframes life as a cyclical journey of awakening rather than a linear pursuit of success. These gates—Falling, Surrendering, Crying, Caring, Hating, Creating, Sharing, Loving, Breathing, and Laughing—each represent a threshold of psychological and spiritual transformation. Drawing from Greek mythology, Biblical narratives, Eastern philosophy, and archetypal storytelling, the book presents a unified map of human development. Its voice combines lyrical prose with intellectual rigor, placing it at the intersection of Joseph Campbell’s mythological insight, Alan Watts’s spiritual inquiry, and the literary introspection of Hermann Hesse.

At a time of accelerating technological change, rising anxiety, and the erosion of traditional sources of meaning, 10 Things to Learn offers something increasingly rare: not just insight, but initiation. It speaks to readers seeking coherence in a fragmented world and restores a sense of purpose through the defining ordeals of the human experience.
